clue.text: Quietly dishes out vegetables

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet, so it stands for quietly
to dish out portions is to allot them

explanation.surface: Someone serving dinner hushed, handing round the greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Small mild bulbs of the onion family, eaten as vegetables.

clue.text: A form of acceptance or resignation

definitions.text: A form of acceptance or resignation

parts.words: A form of acceptance or resignation
parts.note: a set phrase said when one shrugs and accepts what cannot be changed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means let it happen that way, accepting the outcome.

clue.text: The more there are, the fewer are there

definitions.text: The more there are, the fewer are there

parts.words: The more there are, the fewer are there
parts.note: a paradox resolved by people who stay away: each extra one means one fewer present

explanation.definitionFit: People not present; every additional missing person reduces attendance.

clue.text: Shrub I ring up about

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the I
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone telephones about a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub bearing fragrant purple or white flowers.

clue.text: Certain to follow the fashion in hairstyle

indicators.note: the word for certain comes after the word for fashion

parts.note: ton is an old word for the fashion or style
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone is bound to copy the latest haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: A tonsure is the shaved crown worn by monks.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaven crown of a monk is a style of cutting the hair.

clue.text: A hard back for sailors

parts.note: stern means hard or severe

explanation.surface: A tough seaman's back, weathered by years at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: In nautical language astern means behind or towards the rear of a ship.

clue.text: Go to bed in a rough sea, gloomy

indicators.note: the bed phrase is placed within the rearranged sea
a rough sea is churned up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to turn in is to go to bed

explanation.surface: A sailor turns in during a storm, feeling glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to bed' looks like an instruction, but it is the phrase for turning in; 'rough' scrambles the sea and 'in' places the bed phrase within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means sullen and melancholy, a temperament linked with the planet Saturn.

clue.text: Muse to appear after a very long time

indicators.note: the word to comes after the word for a long period

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Inspiration finally strikes after ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Need one tap repaired when the flow is minimal

indicators.note: repairing something puts it back together, here in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A plumber is called because the tap barely trickles.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap tide is the tide of least range, when the tidal flow is smallest.

clue.text: Headquarters' file shows where to find a serving man

definitions.text: where to find a serving man

parts.note: a base is a headquarters
a file of people is a line

explanation.surface: A head office document reveals the whereabouts of a waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'serving man' is a tennis player about to serve, who stands at the back line of the court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the server stands behind the back boundary line of the court.

clue.text: Odd start to A Level

definitions.note: singular in the clue though the answer is a plural noun, layers

indicators.note: something odd is strange or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A peculiar way to begin an A Level exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Level' reads as the British school exam, but the A is fodder and 'Level' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Geological layers of rock, each one a level.

clue.text: Prevent mugs getting knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so in a down clue the word is turned upside down

parts.note: mugs and pots are drinking vessels

explanation.surface: Stop the cups from being toppled.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to halt it.

clue.text: I coin new description of classical architecture

indicators.note: making a new version of the letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have coined a fresh term for ancient building styles.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Greek orders of columns, with scroll-shaped capitals.

clue.text: To hog the conversation is extreme

explanation.surface: Monopolising talk is the furthest one can go.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as two words: to utter most is to do most of the talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak the most monopolises a chat; as one word it means furthest or most extreme.

clue.text: It's safe to view when the dog is kept inside

indicators.note: the dog is held within the word for viewing

parts.note: to see is to view
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A house is safe to inspect once the guard dog is shut in.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe and protected mean the same.

clue.text: Insecure -having not been paid

explanation.surface: A worker feels shaky after going without wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsettled means anxious and unstable; an unsettled bill is one still owing.

clue.text: Showed the way with emphasis

explanation.surface: Someone gave directions forcefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed is the past of indicating a direction; a pointed remark is one made with emphasis.

clue.text: Sheridan's competitors

parts.note: Richard Brinsley Sheridan, the Irish playwright, wrote a comedy whose title means opponents

explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan's 1775 comedy is titled with a word for rivals in competition.

clue.text: I'm only human but never to be forgotten

parts.note: to be mortal is to be only human

explanation.surface: Someone admits frailty yet hopes for lasting fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Deathless fame means a person's memory lives forever.

clue.text: Broods about one's exploits

indicators.note: the brooding word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to brood is to muse
one is I, and the 's gives S

explanation.surface: A worrier considers how they have taken advantage of others.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something can mean to abuse or misapply it.

clue.text: One bound on a crest of a wave, we hear

indicators.note: the phrase says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: surf is the foam on the crest of breaking waves

explanation.surface: A surfer rides on the top of a breaking wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval serf was bound to the land of their lord.

clue.text: Sound conductor of German songs

indicators.note: the word means as heard, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: a conductor is the leader of an orchestra

explanation.surface: A competent maestro of German song recitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic German art songs, as by Schubert, for voice and piano.

clue.text: Data-base?

parts.note: read as two words: data, meaning inside information, and base, meaning a low position

explanation.definitionFit: The inside facts are the full story; something low down is at the base.

clue.text: Balls hit high, right into the heavens

indicators.note: the letter for right goes into the heavenly word

parts.note: the skies are the heavens

explanation.surface: Cricket balls struck high soar straight up into the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a skier is a ball hit high into the air.

clue.text: Cast down by fielding error

explanation.surface: Someone was dejected by a slip in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an overthrow is a fielder's return throw that misses and lets the batters take extra runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple a ruler is to cast them down; in cricket a wild return throw giving away runs is a fielding mistake.

clue.text: Boredom in endless night in France

parts.note: en is the French for in, French signalled by in France

indicators.note: the last letter of the French word is cut off

parts.note: nuit is French for night

explanation.surface: Someone is bored through a long night on a trip to France.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness, a lack of interest.

clue.text: Reflectors are needed for this sort of tank

definitions.text: Reflectors are needed for this sort of tank

parts.words: Reflectors are needed for this sort of tank
parts.note: reflectors are people who reflect, deep ..., and the tank is a body of experts, not a vehicle or water tank

explanation.surface: Mirrors are fitted to a particular kind of tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy research institute is staffed by people who reflect on problems.

clue.text: Not qualified to sum up

explanation.surface: Someone lacks credentials for the job of summarising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not qualified' means absolute, without qualification, not lacking credentials.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete without reservation is unqualified; adding figures together gives their sum.

clue.text: T-junction jam

parts.note: an angle is formed where two lines meet

explanation.surface: Traffic snarled at a T-junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam or snarl is a muddle or knot.

clue.text: After which the participants come out of their shells

definitions.text: After which the participants come out of their shells

parts.words: After which the participants come out of their shells
parts.note: shells are light racing boats, so rowers climb out of them when the event ends, not shy people opening up

explanation.surface: An event that makes the shy blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing contest is raced in shells, narrow racing boats.

clue.text: Number with first-class ways to travel for landowners

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I
RDS is short for roads

explanation.surface: Wealthy estate owners travel only first class.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish holders of landed estates.

clue.text: They should be able to identify any salts in a mixture

definitions.text: They should be able to identify any salts in a mixture

indicators.note: letters in a mixture are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Chemists are expected to recognise the salts in a compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Analytical chemists test a sample to identify the compounds in it.
